question.leadin: This government was headed by Philippe Petain.
question.text: Name this Nazi-approved government that ruled France from a namesake city during World War II, while the Germans occupied Paris.
question.answerHtml: Vichy France [or the French State; or État français; prompt on France]
question.clue: Its secret police was headed by Joseph Darnand after being created by Pierre Laval.

swap.text: English forces under Henry V utilized the longbow during this battle, which took place during St. Crispin's Day. During this battle, French forces under Charles d'Albret got stuck in muddy terrain.
swap.clue: "Double subsidies" raised a fleet of up to 1,500 cogs for the winners of this battle, who attempted to retreat to Calais after taking heavy losses while besieging Harfleur.

question.leadin: Give the following about French diplomat Charles-Maurice de Talleyrand.
question.text: The French Revolution ended with the rise of this friend of Talleyrand as First Consul of France. This manlater became the French Emperor.
question.clue: This man's military expedition in Egypt discovered the Rosetta Stone.

swap.text: An apocryphal legend says that the Rothschild banking family profited from a few hours' advance notice of the Duke of Wellington's victory at this 1815 battle, the final defeat of a certain French emperor.
swap.clue: The absence of General Grouchy deprived the losers of one third of their army.

question.text: An army of these people under Charles Martel prevented the Umayyads from expanding into Western Europe at the Battle of Tours. Shortly after the invasion, they were able to annex the weakened Duchy of Aquitaine.
question.clue: Another ruler of these people waited a year to smash in the head of a man who crushed a bishop's vase.

swap.text: This revolt, partially in response to Danton's execution, ended the Reign of Terror and Robespierre's life.
swap.clue: A target of this event was mysteriously shot in the jaw after being arrested in the Hotel de Ville.

question.leadin: As secretary to Cardinal Mazarin, this man accused Nicolas Fouquet of embezzling funds that had in fact been appropriated by the Cardinal himself.
question.text: Name this 17th-century French finance minister. He promoted a heavily mercantilist policy, including the founding of the French East India Company.
question.clue: His predecessor was Nicolas Fouquet, who was charged with embezzlement due to the charges brought about by this man.

swap.leadin: This ruler divided the land of Francia between his sons Carloman and Pepin.
swap.text: Name this Frankish leader who took a cognomen meaning "The Hammer" after he halted the Muslim advance into Europe in 732.
swap.clue: He served as Mayor of the Palace in Austrasia, a title he passed to his son, Pepin III after securing another victory at the Battle of Cologne.

question.leadin: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, who wrote that "this little island [would] astonish Europe," was later invited to contribute to this island's law code.
question.text: Name this Mediterranean island. In 1755, Pasquale Paoli founded an early Enlightenment republic on this island.
question.clue: An independence leader on this island founded a university at the fortified mountain town of Corte and promulgated a constitution which established a separation of powers and a ban on vendettas.

swap.text: Sentenced to life imprisonment on Devil's Island, Emile Zola's article "J'accuse" was instrumental in swaying public opinion and gaining his release. For fifteen points, name the Jewish French army captain falsely convicted for betraying French secrets in the late 19th century.
swap.clue: The newspaper La Libre Parole frequently attacked this person based on documents that included a "bordereau" discovered in a wastebasket.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the French Revolution.
question.text: This Jacobin and member of the Committee of Public Safety led the Reign of Terror, and was toppled in the Thermidorian reaction.
question.clue: This provincial lawyer from Arras articulated the principles of the Reign of Terror in his 1794 "Report on the Principles of Political Morality" and was guillotined that July.

swap.leadin: Emmanuel Le Roy Ladurie's microhistory of the village of Montaillou studied the records of some of the last people accused of this heresy.
swap.text: Name this heresy, alleged to consist of a dualism between good and evil, supposedly led by a spiritual elite known as the perfecti.
swap.clue: Emmanuel Le Roy Ladurie examines the methodic search for members of this heresy in the title town of his work Montaillou.

question.leadin: Historian Marc Bloch first used his method of combining historical sources with research in the social sciences in a book about beliefs surrounding these people.
question.text: Name these people, who were believed to have the miraculous power to cure the disease scrofula through their namesake "touch." The anointing of these people's hands was traditionally performed at Reims Cathedral.
question.answerHtml: kings [accept Les Rois thaumaturges; accept kings of France or French kings]
question.clue: The Sumerians kept poetic lists of these people called lugal, or "big man". In those lists, there could only be one of these people in Mesopotamia at once, and a sequence of them from the same city formed a dynasty.

swap.leadin: This treaty followed the battles of Saint-Quentin and Gravelines, and it transferred land to Emmanuel-Philibert.
swap.text: Name this 1559 treaty, which confirmed Spanish control of much of Italy and was signed by Henry II of France.
swap.clue: Prior to signing this treaty, one monarch who was party to it sent a memorandum to his sister Joanna claiming that his presence in Flanders was necessary to prevent a possible invasion of England.

question.leadin: Lewis Mumford argues that this man's urban renewal projects were not for the good of the city, but instead made it easier to crush popular uprisings.
question.text: Name this baron, whom Napoleon III appointed Prefect of the Seine, with his main task to fully renovate Paris. He bulldozed buildings in the historic center to build large boulevards, including one named for him.
question.clue: This "Baron," who was tasked by Napoleon III to carry out a massive renovation program for the capital city; critics found this man's work too extravagant.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about European countries where communists and democratic governments got along, if briefly.
swap.text: During Republic-era Spain, the communists joined with the socialists and other left-wing parties to form this party for the 1936 elections, which won and installed Manuel Azana as president.
swap.clue: Meetings that this government conducted with trade unions resulted in the Matignon accords, which granted a 40-hour work week.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about a French monarch and his reign.
question.text: This son of Blanche of Castile repelled revolts by Raymond VII of Toulouse and eventually signed a treaty of Paris with Henry III of England.
question.clue: This king of France who led the Seventh and Eighth Crusades.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about historiographic reactions to COVID-19.
swap.text: Many historians have used the title of this historian's book Strange Defeat to describe the failure of Western governments during COVID-19. This Jewish member of the Annales school was executed for activities in the French Resistance.
swap.clue: A study by this man, which documented popular belief in a cure for scrofula, was titled The Royal Touch.

question.leadin: Answer the following about 1848 in France, FTPE.
question.text: Making his name fighting in Algeria, this general arrived in Paris and used martial law to put down the bloody June Days uprising. He opposed Louis Napoleon Bonaparte during the subsequent presidential election and was handily defeated.
question.clue: The July closure of Louis Blanc's national workshops inspired a working-class uprising which was violently quelled by this man, who later ran for President of France against Louis-Napoleon.

swap.text: A 721 siege of this city was also a major blow to the Muslim conquest of Europe. Malik al-Khawlani besieged it for three months until his forces were defeated by Duke Odo of Aquitaine.
